newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga raises oil, gas reserves by 27 pct.
newsitem.headline: Saga raises oil, gas reserves by 27 pct.

text.p: Saga Petroleum ASA said on Wednesday it had increased its proved and probable reserves by 27 percent in 1996 to 1.438 billion barrels of oil equivalent (boe), evenly distributed between oil and gas.
"This is a net increase of 305 million boe for the year," Saga said in a statement annoucing its annual results.
The growth in the group's reserves excluding acquisitions was equivalent to 347 percent of the reserves produced in the year, it said. Similarly oil production in 1996 was replaced by 204 percent.
At the end of the year, Saga's remaining proved reserves were 951 million boe compared with 791 million boe for the preceding year.

The company said that in addition to its acquisition of UK-based offshore group Santa Fe Exploration, the growth in reserves largely came from the Varg, Oseberg Syd, Troll, Snorre and Gullfaks fields on the Norwegian continental shelf.
Norway's largest listed oil company booked pre-tax profits before extraordinary items up 72 percent at 3.47 billion crowns against 2.02 billion crowns in 1995.
Operating profits jumped 78 percent to 3.32 billion crowns versus 1.86 billion crowns.
